mainTopic: The meaning of "כלל גדול" in the משנה, and רב and שמואל on who counts as forgetting the essence of שבת
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about how many חטאות a person brings for doing מלאכה on שבת. The גמרא then asks why the משנה opened with the words "כלל גדול." A first answer, that "גדול" is used because a second principle comes later, fails because of מעשר. A second answer from רבי יוסי בר אבין, that "גדול" goes with areas of law that have אבות and תולדות, fails because of בר קפרא's version of the משנה. The answer that holds is that "גדול" means wider in scope: שבת covers more than שביעית, and שביעית covers more than מעשר. For בר קפרא, מעשר is also "גדול" because it covers figs and vegetables, which פאה does not, and the גמרא proves this by comparing the conditions for פאה with the conditions for מעשר. Then רב and שמואל explain that the משנה's "one who forgets the essence of שבת" means someone who never knew about שבת, like a captured child or a convert among non-Jews. The גמרא defends their view against two challenges by rereading the words "השוכח" and "היודע."

steps.title: End of the משנה: Many labors of one type bring only one offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by teaching that doing many labors that all belong to one category of מלאכה brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: [He is liable] for each and every main category of labor. A person who does many labors that all belong to one category of labor is liable to bring only one sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the משנה, which opened with "כלל גדול אמרו בשבת" (on the previous amud). It finishes listing when a person brings one חטאת and when he brings many.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The count of חטאות goes by categories (אבות מלאכה), not by actions. If someone does several different main categories, he brings one חטאת for each. If all his actions fall under one category, they count as one sin, and he brings one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A main category of forbidden labor on שבת (one of the 39)
Of the same type as one category of labor
A sin-offering brought for doing a sin by mistake

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole idea of אבות and תולדות. The גמרא will use that idea in step 5.

phrases.english: for each and every primary category of labor.
phrases.notes: Finishes the previous line of the משנה: he is liable for each main category he did.

phrases.english: One who performs many labors
that are of the type of one category of labor,
is liable to bring only one sin-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹשֶׂה מְלָאכוֹת הַרְבֵּה מֵעֵין מְלָאכָה אַחַת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Many labors within one category bring only one חטאת. Separate categories each bring their own חטאת.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say "a great principle"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the משנה used the word "גדול" (great) when it said "כלל גדול."
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the reason the משנה taught "a great principle"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks about a word in the משנה. Why did it call this principle "great" instead of just "a principle"?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes every word in a משנה has a purpose. Calling a rule "גדול" must mean something. The question asks what that extra word adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
What is the reason?
A great (or major) principle
He (the תנא, author of the משנה) taught

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What is the reason the mishna taught "a great principle"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording that opened the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the word "גדול" adds in the phrase "כלל גדול"

steps.title: First suggestion: "Great" is used because another principle comes later
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the משנה says "כלל גדול" because it will later say "עוד כלל אחר אמרו." The same pattern appears in שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because the משנה wants to teach later "They said another principle," so here it taught "a great principle"; and with שביעית too, because it wants to teach "They said another principle," it taught "a great principle."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer, starting with "אילימא" (if you say). It is setting up an answer that it will soon attack.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that "גדול" just tells us this is the first and bigger principle, because a second one follows. The same pattern appears in מסכת שביעית, which also says "כלל גדול" and later "עוד כלל אחר." So far the theory fits both places.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say: introduces a suggestion the גמרא will likely reject
They said yet another principle
The seventh (שמיטה) year, and the מסכת about it

steps.confusionAlert: The word "אילימא" means this answer is only a suggestion. Do not treat it as the final answer. The גמרא is about to challenge it.

phrases.english: If you say it is because he wants to teach [later]:
"Furthermore, they said another principle,"
[therefore] he taught "a great principle."
And with regard to the Sabbatical Year as well,
because he wants to teach [later]:
"Furthermore, they said another principle,"
[therefore] he taught "a great principle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "גדול" marks the first principle because a second principle ("כלל אחר") follows later.

steps.title: Challenge from מעשר: Another principle follows, but no "great"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the first suggestion. In מעשר, the משנה says "כלל אחר אמרו" but never says "כלל גדול."
steps.simpleTranslation: But with regard to מעשר, it teaches "They said another principle," and it does not teach "a great principle"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion from step 3. It uses מסכת מעשרות as a counter-example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If "גדול" were used whenever a second principle follows, the משנה in מעשרות should also say "כלל גדול." It also has a second principle, but it only says "כלל אמרו." So the presence of a second principle cannot be the reason for the word "גדול."

keyTerms.meaning: But look: introduces a challenge
Tithes, the portion of produce that must be separated
With regard to

phrases.english: But with regard to tithes,
where it teaches: "They said another principle,"
and it does not teach "a great principle"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 3 with a counter-example
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that "גדול" is used because a second principle follows
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשרות has a second principle but no "גדול," so the suggested reason does not work.

steps.title: רבי יוסי בר אבין: "Great" is used where there are אבות and תולדות
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי בר אבין explains that שבת and שביעית have אבות and תולדות, so they get "גדול." מעשר has no such structure, so it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי בר אבין said: For שבת and שביעית, which have אבות and תולדות, he taught "great." For מעשר, which has no אבות and תולדות, he did not teach "a great principle."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי בר אבין gives a new reason for the word "גדול." It explains why מעשר is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason is about the content of the laws, not the order of the principles. שבת and שביעית have main labors (אבות) and labors derived from them (תולדות), so their rules are "bigger." מעשר has no such categories, so its principle is not called "גדול."

keyTerms.meaning: Main categories (of forbidden actions)
Subcategories: actions that come from a main category
There is not

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei bar Avin said:
Shabbat and the Sabbatical Year,
which have main categories and subcategories —
he taught "great."
Tithes, which do not have main categories and subcategories,
he did not teach "a great principle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4 with a new explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "גדול" depends on whether a second principle follows
steps.terutzMaskana: "גדול" depends on whether the area of law has אבות and תולדות

steps.title: Challenge from בר קפרא's version: "Great" appears in מעשר too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוסי בר אבין. In בר קפרא's version of the משנה, מעשר does say "כלל גדול," yet it has no אבות and תולדות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בר קפרא, who teaches "a great principle" regarding מעשר, what אבות and what תולדות are there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 5. It uses another version of the text, taught by בר קפרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בר קפרא's version of the משנה in מעשרות reads "כלל גדול." But מעשר has no אבות and תולדות. So the theory of step 5 cannot explain that wording.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there? (asked rhetorically, meaning: there is none)

phrases.english: And according to Bar Kappara,
who teaches "a great principle" with regard to tithes,
what main categories and what subcategories are there?

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי בר אבין's theory that "גדול" depends on אבות and תולדות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בר קפרא uses "גדול" for מעשר, which has no אבות and תולדות, so the theory fails for his version.

steps.title: Real reason: שבת covers more than שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a new reason. "גדול" means wider in scope. שבת applies to both detached and attached things. שביעית applies only to what is attached to the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this the reason: the punishment of שבת is greater than that of שביעית. שבת applies both to detached and to attached things, while שביעית does not apply to detached things; it applies to attached things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier answers and gives a new explanation. "גדול" is a comparison: each area of law is "greater" in scope than the next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת you can be liable for actions on things already picked (תלוש) and on things still growing (מחובר). The laws of שביעית apply only to working the land and its growing plants. So שבת's principle is "greater" than שביעית's because it covers more.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, isn't this the reason: introduces the true explanation
Its punishment (here: the range of things for which one can be punished)
Detached: picked off the ground
Attached: still growing in the ground

steps.confusionAlert: "גדול עונשה" does not mean the punishment is harsher. It means the law covers a wider range of things.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this the reason:
the punishment of Shabbat is greater
than that of the Sabbatical Year,
for Shabbat applies
both to detached and to attached things,
whereas the Sabbatical Year does not apply to detached things,
[but] it applies to attached things.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 5 with a new reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "גדול" depends on having אבות and תולדות
steps.terutzMaskana: "גדול" means the area of law has wider scope than the next one

steps.title: Second link: שביעית covers more than מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The answer continues. שביעית applies to both human food and animal food. מעשר applies only to human food.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the punishment of שביעית is greater than that of מעשר, for שביעית applies to both human food and animal food, whereas מעשר applies to human food but does not apply to animal food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא completes the chain of comparisons: שבת is greater than שביעית, and שביעית is greater than מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of שביעית apply to produce eaten by people and to produce eaten by animals. מעשר applies only to food for people. This also explains בר קפרא: מעשר can be called "גדול" compared to an area of law even smaller than it.

keyTerms.meaning: Human food
Animal food
It applies (literally: it is there)

steps.whatToRemember: "כלל גדול" is a relative term meaning wider in scope. שבת (detached and attached) is greater than שביעית (attached only, but both human and animal food), and שביעית is greater than מעשר (human food only).

phrases.english: And the punishment of the Sabbatical Year is greater
than that of tithes,
for the Sabbatical Year applies

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּמַאֲכַל אָדָם בֵּין בְּמַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה,
phrases.english: both to human food and to animal food,
whereas tithes apply to human food
[but] do not apply to animal food.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְגָדוֹל עוֹנְשָׁהּ שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית יוֹתֵר מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the comparison chain begun in step 7
steps.terutzMaskana: Each area of law is "גדול" relative to the one below it in scope
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: "גדול" describes relative breadth: שבת is greater than שביעית, and שביעית is greater than מעשר.

steps.title: For בר קפרא, מעשר is wider than פאה
steps.stepSummary: Following the 'wider scope' idea, the גמרא explains that בר קפרא calls מעשר 'גדול' because it applies to figs and vegetables, while פאה does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בר קפרא, who teaches 'a great principle' about מעשר: the punishment of מעשר is greater than that of פאה. מעשר applies to figs and vegetables, but פאה does not apply to figs and vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its new answer. It shows how בר קפרא's wording also fits: מעשר is 'גדול' compared to פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the גמרא said 'גדול' means wider in scope. Now that idea solves the question from בר קפרא in Step 6. מעשר covers figs and vegetables and פאה does not, so מעשר is wider. That is why בר קפרא can call it 'גדול'.

keyTerms.meaning: its punishment; here it means the range of things for which one can be punished
the corner of the field left for the poor
fig
vegetable

steps.whyThisMatters: It completes the chain: שבת is wider than שביעית, שביעית is wider than מעשר, and מעשר is wider than פאה. Each one is 'גדול' compared to the one below it.

phrases.english: And according to bar Kappara, who teaches 'a great principle' regarding tithes:
the punishment of tithes is greater
than that of pe'a,
since tithes apply to figs and vegetables
while pe'a does not apply to figs and vegetables.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְבַר קַפָּרָא דְּתָנֵי כְּלָל גָּדוֹל בַּמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the 'wider scope' answer and applies it one level further down, to מעשר versus פאה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the new definition of 'גדול' to answer the challenge from בר קפרא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without אבות and תולדות, מעשר seemed to have no reason to be called 'גדול'.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר is 'גדול' because it covers figs and vegetables, which פאה does not.

steps.title: The משנה listing the conditions for פאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה in פאה, which lists five conditions for produce to need פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: They stated a rule about פאה. Anything that is food, is guarded, grows from the ground, is picked all at once, and is brought in for storage, must have פאה left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to prove that פאה does not apply to figs and vegetables. It quotes the five conditions for פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something needs פאה only if it meets all five conditions. The last two conditions, 'picked all at once' and 'brought in for storage', will turn out to leave out figs and vegetables.

keyTerms.meaning: and it is guarded, meaning it has an owner
it is picked all at once
and one brings it in to store it for a long time

phrases.english: As we learned: They stated a principle regarding pe'a:
Anything that is food and is guarded
and grows from the ground
and is picked all at once
and one brings it in for storage
is obligated in pe'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source for the claim in Step 9 that פאה does not apply to figs and vegetables.
steps.raayaObject: That פאה does not apply to figs and vegetables
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת פאה listing five conditions

steps.title: What each condition of פאה leaves out
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains what each of the five conditions excludes. 'Picked all at once' excludes figs, and 'brought in for storage' excludes vegetables.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Food' leaves out dye plants like woad and madder. 'Guarded' leaves out ownerless produce. 'Grows from the ground' leaves out truffles and mushrooms. 'Picked all at once' leaves out figs. 'Brought in for storage' leaves out vegetables.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the list one condition at a time. It shows exactly which item each condition takes out of פאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key point for our sugya is the last two lines. Figs ripen at different times, so they are not picked all at once. Vegetables spoil quickly, so they are not stored. That is why פאה does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: to exclude, to leave out
aftergrowth of woad and madder, plants used for dye and not for food
ownerless property
truffles and mushrooms

phrases.english: 'Food' excludes aftergrowths of woad and madder.
'And guarded' excludes ownerless produce.

phrases.aramaic: וְגִידּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ — לְמַעוֹטֵי כְּמֵיהִין וּפִטְרִיּוֹת.
phrases.english: 'And grows from the ground' excludes truffles and mushrooms.
phrases.notes: They do not draw their food from the ground.

phrases.english: 'And picked all at once' excludes the fig.
phrases.notes: Figs ripen over a long period of time.

phrases.english: 'And brought in for storage' excludes vegetables.
phrases.notes: Vegetables do not keep for long.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains each condition of the משנה quoted in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Figs and vegetables are not subject to פאה, because they are not picked all at once and are not stored.

steps.title: The מעשר rule has only three conditions
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about מעשר lists only the first three conditions. Figs and vegetables therefore need מעשר, which makes מעשר wider than פאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about מעשר we learned: They stated a rule about מעשר. Anything that is food, is guarded, and grows from the ground must be tithed. 'Picked all at once' and 'brought in for storage' were not taught.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא compares the two lists and finishes the proof. The מעשר list is missing the two conditions that left out figs and vegetables.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fewer conditions means more produce is included. Figs and vegetables need מעשר even though they do not need פאה. This proves that מעשר is wider, so בר קפרא can call it 'גדול'.

keyTerms.meaning: regarding, in the case of
we did not learn it; it is not in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: 'גדול' means wider in scope. שבת is wider than שביעית, שביעית is wider than מעשר, and for בר קפרא מעשר is wider than פאה, because figs and vegetables need מעשר but not פאה.

phrases.english: Whereas regarding tithes we learned:
They stated a principle regarding tithes:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל שֶׁהוּא אוֹכֶל וְנִשְׁמָר וְגִידּוּלוֹ מִן הָאָרֶץ —
phrases.english: Anything that is food, is guarded, and grows from the ground
is obligated in tithes.
But 'picked all at once' and 'brought in for storage'
we did not learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 10 by setting the מעשר list against the פאה list.
steps.raayaObject: That מעשר applies to figs and vegetables, so it is wider than פאה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in מסכת מעשרות listing only three conditions

steps.title: רב and שמואל: our משנה means someone who never knew about שבת
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל explain that 'one who forgets the essence of שבת' refers to a child captured by non-Jews or a convert who converted among non-Jews. Someone who once knew and then forgot is liable for every שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: Our משנה is about a child taken captive among non-Jews and a convert who converted among non-Jews. But someone who knew and later forgot is liable for each and every שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to our משנה and its phrase 'one who forgets the essence of שבת'. רב and שמואל explain which kind of person this means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says such a person brings only one חטאת for all the שבתות he violated. רב and שמואל limit this to someone who never knew about שבת at all. A person who once knew about שבת and then forgot is treated like one who knows, so he brings a חטאת for each שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: both of them
a child taken captive and raised without knowing Torah
a convert who converted while living among non-Jews and was never taught
he knew and in the end forgot

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'liable for each and every שבת' means he must bring a separate חטאת for each שבת. It is a more severe result than the one חטאת for someone who never knew.

phrases.english: It is Rav and Shmuel who both say:
Our mishna is about a child taken captive among the gentiles,
and a convert who converted among the gentiles.
But one who knew and in the end forgot
is liable for each and every Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'כלל גדול' discussion and starts a new topic: what case the משנה means by forgetting the essence of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only someone who never knew about שבת brings one חטאת for all of them. Someone who knew and then forgot brings one for each שבת.

steps.title: Challenge: 'forgets' means he once knew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב and שמואל. The word 'forgets' seems to show that the person once knew about שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'One who forgets the essence of שבת.' Doesn't this show that he knew about it at first?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב and שמואל using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You can only forget something you once knew. So the משנה seems to be describing exactly the 'knew and forgot' person. Yet רב and שמואל said that person is liable for every שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the basic existence of שבת
doesn't this imply
knowledge at the beginning

phrases.english: We learned: 'One who forgets the essence of Shabbat,'
doesn't this imply that he had
knowledge originally?!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הַשּׁוֹכֵחַ עִיקַּר שַׁבָּת, לָאו מִכְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of רב and שמואל from Step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and שמואל's claim that the משנה refers only to someone who never knew about שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word 'השוכח' (forgets) suggests earlier knowledge, which contradicts their reading.

steps.title: 'Forgets' means שבת was always forgotten from him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'השוכח' means שבת was always forgotten from him, meaning he never knew it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What does 'one who forgets the essence of שבת' mean? That the essence of שבת was forgotten from him, meaning hidden from him all along.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב and שמואל by reading the word 'forgets' differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שוכח' here does not mean he knew and then lost the knowledge. It describes a state in which שבת was never in his mind. So the משנה fits the captive child and the convert, as רב and שמואל said.

keyTerms.meaning: forgotten from him, unknown to him

steps.whatToRemember: For רב and שמואל, only someone who never knew about שבת brings one חטאת for all the שבתות. 'השוכח' simply means שבת was never known to him.

phrases.english: No. What is the meaning of 'anyone who forgets the essence of Shabbat'?
That it was forgotten from him,
the essence of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, מַאי כׇּל הַשּׁוֹכֵחַ עִיקַּר שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14 by reinterpreting the word 'השוכח'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Forgets' implies he once knew about שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Forgets' means שבת was always unknown to him, which fits רב and שמואל.

steps.title: Why doesn't the משנה teach the case of someone who knew and then forgot?
steps.stepSummary: According to רב ושמואל, someone who knew שבת and then forgot it is liable for every שבת. If so, the משנה should have taught that case, and the case of someone who simply knows שבת would follow even more strongly.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now take someone who knew שבת and later forgot it. What is the law? Is he liable for each and every שבת? If so, look at the next line of the משנה: 'One who knows the essence of שבת and did many labors on many שבתות is liable for each and every שבת.' Instead of that, the משנה should say 'one who knew and later forgot.' Then we would know, all the more so, that someone who still knows is liable too.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ושמואל again, this time using the wording of the next case in the משנה. It argues that under their reading, the משנה chose the wrong example to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ושמואל said that someone who knew and then forgot is liable for each שבת. That is a new and surprising point. Someone who still knows שבת is obviously liable too, so a משנה should teach the bigger news and let the obvious case follow by קל וחומר. Since the משנה teaches only the obvious case, it seems the 'knew and forgot' ruling is not what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: He knew, and in the end he forgot
Instead of teaching
Let it teach (it should have said)
And all the more so (the obvious case follows)
Many forbidden labors

steps.confusionAlert: The first question ('what is the law?') is not a real request for information. The גמרא already knows רב ושמואל's answer: he is liable for every שבת. It asks the question only to set up the challenge from the משנה's wording.

phrases.english: But one who knew and ultimately forgot, what is the law?
Is he liable for each and every Shabbat?
phrases.notes: This is the conclusion that follows from רב ושמואל's view.

phrases.english: Instead of teaching: one who knows the essence of Shabbat
and performed many labors
on many Shabbatot
is liable for each and every Shabbat
let it teach: 'one who knew and ultimately forgot'
and all the more so this one (the one who still knows)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּתָנֵי הַיּוֹדֵעַ עִיקַּר שַׁבָּת לִיתְנֵי הִכִּיר וּלְבַסּוֹף שָׁכַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 15 defended רב ושמואל's reading of 'השוכח'. Now the גמרא raises a second challenge, based on the wording of the משנה's next case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ושמואל's ruling that someone who knew and then forgot is liable for every שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה should teach the more surprising case and let the obvious case follow by קל וחומר. Here the משנה teaches only the obvious case of someone who still knows, so it seems not to hold the 'knew and forgot' ruling.

steps.title: 'One who knows' means one who knew and then forgot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reinterprets the משנה. The phrase 'one who knows the essence of שבת' refers to someone who once knew it and later forgot it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'one who knows the essence of שבת' mean? It means someone who used to know the essence of שבת and then forgot it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by rereading the משנה's words. The משנה really does teach the 'knew and forgot' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that 'היודע' means someone who knows שבת right now. The answer reads it as 'someone who had the knowledge' in the past and then forgot it. So the משנה does teach the new case, and רב ושמואל's view fits the משנה after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The essence (basic existence) of שבת
Who used to know
And forgot it

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב ושמואל, the משנה has two levels. 'השוכח' is someone who never knew שבת at all (a captured child or a convert among non-Jews). 'היודע' is someone who once knew שבת and later forgot it. The first is less liable than the second, who is liable for every שבת.
steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the defense of רב ושמואל. Both challenges, from 'השוכח' and from 'היודע', are answered by reading the words carefully, so their view fits the משנה's language.

phrases.english: What is the meaning of 'one who knows the essence of Shabbat'?

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁהָיָה יוֹדֵעַ עִיקָּרָהּ שֶׁל שַׁבָּת וּשְׁכֵחָהּ
phrases.english: One who used to know the essence of Shabbat and forgot it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This directly answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought 'היודע' meant someone who knows שבת right now, so the 'knew and forgot' case seemed missing from the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'היודע' means someone who once knew שבת and then forgot it. So the משנה does teach the new case, in line with רב ושמואל.
